provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program finds the 4-connected components of the colour palette[3] (the original colour 3) in the grid it is given. It counts the ones that have exactly 4 cells and a 2x2 bounding box. Rotating or reflecting a solid 2x2 square leaves it a solid 2x2 square, so the count is the same in every orientation. The output is a 3x3 grid filled with palette[0]. One cell is set to palette[1] for each counted square, up to 3. In the original task these cells run down the main diagonal, filled from the top-left: (0,0), (1,1), (2,2). The factory works out where those three cells land under the given transform, using the same steps as the spec. For d4>=4 it first mirrors the column (c -> 2-c). It then rotates clockwise d4%4 times, each time mapping (r,c) -> (c, 2-r). It writes the resulting cells into the program as constants, in their original fill order. So, for example, a reflection produces an anti-diagonal filled from the top-right. Colour 2 squares and stray cells are ignored, as in the original rule. Demonstrations are not needed and are not used.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the palette maps distinct colours to distinct colours, so that palette[3] identifies only the original colour-3 cells. This matches the generator's domain: colour-3 boxes never overlap or touch one another, and there are always 1 to 3 colour-3 2x2 squares. If more than 3 squares appear, the program caps the count at 3, as the archived solver does. The fixtures agree with this uniform rule. No tests were run.
